acceptance: The Presto-family 1_v7 text builds one array of ROW values (alignment intrinsic) and, by the harness at a recorded clean commit, passes at SF1, SF2 and SF3 on Trino under stock limits (1.80 GB per node on a 6 GiB heap) with results equal to canonical Q1 within 1e-8; SF3 fails today

Peak user memory per run is recorded for each scale and compared with the 760-835 MiB per SF baseline in _project/audits/tpchavoc-q1-array-scale-2026-10-22.md; the ORDER BY keep-or-drop decision is made from those harness numbers
Presto, Trino and Athena rendering assertions (tests/unit/tpchavoc/test_presto_compat.py and the sql_compat golden corpus entries for 1_v7) describe the new shape
The 1_v7 variant description or docs state that memory is linear in rows of the largest Q1 group, and the owner decision on a documented requirement versus a scale-gated skip is recorded
description: The 1_v7 text for Presto, Trino and Athena (the fork's order_list_aggregates + reduce_list_aggregates rewrites: four ordered ARRAY_AGG columns reduced with REDUCE/ZIP_WITH, develop #3326) exceeds Trino's default per-node memory limit from SF3. On Trino 484 with a 6 GiB heap it passes at SF1 (about 800 MiB) and SF2 (about 1.6 GiB, 87% of the 1843 MiB cap) and fails with EXCEEDED_LOCAL_MEMORY_LIMIT at SF3 and SF10, while canonical Q1 needs under 16 MiB. Memory is linear in rows, 760-835 MiB per scale factor, dominated by HashAggregationOperator ARRAY_AGG state. See the context of tpchavoc-q1-array-scale-check and _project/audits/tpchavoc-q1-array-scale-2026-10-22.md (merged in PR 3310). A probe on the earlier UNNEST text showed one ARRAY_AGG of ROW values cut peak memory about 1.7-1.9x, whereas chunking by GROUP BY or UNION ALL slicing gave no reduction; that factor is not yet re-tested on the current REDUCE text. This does not make memory bounded. Do not claim more. The rewrite lives in the fork, so the change is a fork/rule change plus a BenchBox pin.
